items.description: Squash racket in the dominant hand. WSF racket specification (see worldsquash.sport/racket-specification): maximum length 686 mm, maximum width 215 mm, maximum strung area 500 cm2, maximum weight 255 g.

dimensions.note: Figures from the WSF racket specification as reproduced by secondary sources; TODO_REQUIRES_VALIDATION against the current WSF page before any rule use.

items.note: Racket head tracking (SAM 2 object track or point track on the head) enables swing-path, racket-preparation height and estimated-contact criteria; without it those criteria abstain.

items.description: WSF specification ball; competition ball is the double yellow dot (slowest). Nominal diameter 40.0 +/- 0.5 mm, mass 24 +/- 1 g; dot colours indicate speed/bounce (double yellow, yellow, red, blue).

dimensions.note: TODO_REQUIRES_VALIDATION: confirm rebound resilience and tolerances on worldsquash.sport/ball-specification.

items.note: A 40 mm black ball at up to 60 m/s is not trackable live by phone cameras; offline deep analysis may attempt it from high frame-rate video. Bounce and wall-contact events needed for faults and lets are not inferred from pose.

items.description: Protective eyewear to a national standard (for example ASTM F803/F3164, BS 7930.1, AS/NZS 4066, CSA P400); recommended for all play, mandatory in WSF doubles and junior events (Rules Appendix 4).
items.note: May occlude eye landmarks; criteria never use face landmarks.

items.description: 50 mm floor and wall lines (short line, half-court line, service boxes, service line, front wall line, back wall line, tin top).
items.note: Calibration target: detecting the short line, half-court line and service boxes lets the perception layer map image coordinates to the court frame (metres) for T-position and lunge-reach criteria.

items.description: Transparent back wall (2.13 m or higher) common on show and club courts.
items.note: Reflections of players and spectators in glass walls create false detections; filter detections outside the court polygon after calibration (Brumann et al. 2021).
